column2: Creating a CPU using the RISC-V ISA, with a goal of running a Linux system and eventually run a 2simple 2D/3D game.

column4: The Linux-capable CPU core with an MMU uses ~15k LUTs. You also need space for the display controller and SDRAM/DDR3 controllers.
Linux takes roughly 24MB to 32MB just to sit at the terminal. Doom needs another 8MB of working memory, plus a dedicated frame buffer for the display.
A standard 8-bit SPI PSRAM chip is too slow. The CPU will stall trying to fetch Linux instructions and draw Doom frames simultaneously.
To hold your Linux root filesystem, the compiled Linux kernel, and the DOOM.WAD game asset file.
